hypotheses.title: Field-verified BRIDGE LiDAR faults as bounded analog-source supervision
layers: BRIDGE GIS fault picks from GDR submission 1682 (source line labels, field-verified only in Dixie Valley and Gabbs Valley per its official README)
GeoDAWN training features: tmi_hg (band 3), tmi_vg (9), det_elev (12), det_elev_slope (19), iso_grav_anom_hg (18), depth_to_base_surf (15)
hypotheses.physical_signature: A multi-scale, orientation-preserving lineament/edge response in magnetic, gravity, basement-surface and terrain layers, trained/checked against the source's mapped fault polylines. Transfer is only considered after the shared-layer domain discriminator and spatially blocked source/target tests.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: The GDR BRIDGE README describes LiDAR fault picks that were field verified in Dixie Valley and Gabbs Valley. Those mapped scarps are an independent source label population; they can test whether the feature signature of a field-mapped fault appears beyond the published regional catalogue. They are not assumed to be new target faults, and they are not used as a score label without spatial/geographic holdout.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: Earlier H19/H27/H36/H38 artifacts use the same regional fault catalogue and/or LiDAR-derived scarp features as predictors. No reviewed earlier artifact used BRIDGE field-verified fault picks as independent source labels or measured transfer divergence against them.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium (official GIS archive lists 3.79 MB; reprojection, attribution checks, exact footprint overlap, deduplication and spatial holdout still needed)
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: DOE Geothermal Data Repository submission 1682, https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1682; direct GIS file https://gdr.openei.org/files/1682/BRIDGE_GIS.zip; README https://gdr.openei.org/files/1682/BRIDGE_README.pdf
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Official page fetch succeeded 2026-10-04. It marks the submission public and CC BY 4.0 and lists GIS Files.zip at 3.79 MB. README says LiDAR fault picks were field verified only in Dixie Valley and Gabbs Valley. Local curl to the file URL failed TLS (HTTP 000); bytes not staged or inspected.
hypotheses.status: BLOCKED — do not call viable or run transfer until the official archive is downloaded, hash-recorded, feature schema/CRS/coverage inspected, and all share-to-sponsor terms confirmed. No holdout or slot run.

hypotheses.title: USGS ComCat focal-mechanism orientation prior for active lineaments
layers: USGS ComCat focal-mechanism product: event location plus nodal-plane strike/dip/rake
GeoDAWN tmi_hg (3), tmi_vg (9), det_elev (12), det_elev_slope (19), geod_2ndinv (4), geod_shearrate (7), geod_dilaterate (8)
hypotheses.physical_signature: An orientation-conditioned line filter: reward candidate magnetic/geomorphic lineaments whose azimuth and dip direction are mechanically compatible with nearby, reviewed normal/strike-slip focal mechanisms; do not rasterize earthquake density as a fault label.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: Focal mechanisms constrain active seismogenic slip planes from waveform radiation patterns rather than from the surface fault traces compiled in USGS/INGENIOUS. A lineament consistent with those mechanisms but absent from the surface inventory is a candidate for an unmapped or blind structure.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: GEMSDOE32 H61-2 proposed seismicity-density ridge/coherence, and supplied band 16 is earthquake intensity/density. This uses individual event focal-plane geometry, not density or proximity alone.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium (API harvesting, duplicate-event/product resolution, uncertainty filters, spatially blocked evaluation)
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: USGS ANSS ComCat docs https://earthquake.usgs.gov/data/comcat/index.php and FDSN query API https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Official API count query returned 6,168 focal-mechanism products in the approximate footprint for M>=2.5 and 233 for M>=4 through 2026-10-04. A fetched example event product contains nodal-plane strike/dip/rake. Local curl failed TLS (HTTP 000), so a full response was not saved locally.
hypotheses.status: DESK-CHECKED SOURCE; not locally harvested, not validated, not viable for submission yet.

hypotheses.title: Brady–Desert Peak alteration/structure coincidence (mineral layers unconfirmed)
layers: Candidate alteration/mineral indicator layers, if present in DOE GDR submission 1303; the official listing does not confirm a hyperspectral product or these layer semantics, and the archive has not been inspected
GeoDAWN tmi_hg (3), iso_grav_anom_hg (18), det_elev (12) and existing LiDAR-scarp channels
hypotheses.physical_signature: If the official archive contains quality-controlled silica/clay/evaporite mineral-assemblage layers, test whether their contact/halo boundaries coincide with independent magnetic/gravity/terrain lineaments rather than using raw K/Th/U amplitude. If those layers are absent or semantically unsuitable, retire the hypothesis instead of substituting an unverified proxy.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: Hydrothermal alteration can mark long-lived permeability and upflow above blind faults without requiring a preserved Quaternary scarp. A spatial association with an independent structural edge is more specific than alteration alone.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: H35-1 used hot spring/well temperatures, one quartz geothermometry threshold, radiometric masks and Euler proximity; H38-1 used conductive heat-flow residual plus Euler. This hypothesis would test verified mineral-assemblage/contact layers with an independent edge-coincidence gate, if those layers actually exist in GDR 1303. No such layer is confirmed or used here.
hypotheses.expected_DTI_improvement_rank: low-to-moderate; plausible only as a strict structural conjunction
hypotheses.implementation_cost: high (official page lists a 2.58 GB multi-site DOE geodatabase; geodatabase extraction, CRS/coverage, pixel scale and mineral-class semantics need audit)
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: DOE GDR submission 1303, https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1303; DOE_GDB.zip link listed as https://gdr.openei.org/files/1303/DOE_GDB.zip
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Official page fetched 2026-10-04; public, CC BY 4.0, lists the 2.58 GB geodatabase for Brady, Desert Peak and Salton Sea. The archive was not downloaded, so overlap and raster schemas remain unknown.
hypotheses.status: BLOCKED — do not call the mineral/hyperspectral layers available; inspect the official archive, layer schema, footprint overlap, provenance and license conditions first.

promotion_policy: The D2.8 owner-mirror is the only ready reference file. No new candidate is promoted in this session. A new transfer candidate must be evaluated on spatially withheld fault systems with the prediction built without the held-out geometry, use an independently defined matched-comparison budget, and beat a current-best comparable artifact in fresh confirmation. A local catalogue holdout is a proxy for generalization among mapped faults, not a test of the competition's absent/hidden fault population.
